# Neptune

**Parity grade: A** · SDK `aws-sdk-go-v2/service/neptune@v1.53.3` · last audited 2026-10-12 (`0c1472972`)

## Coverage

### Known gaps

- UNVERIFIABLE: OrderableDBInstanceOption.SupportedNetworkTypes stays empty; the pinned SDK states no per-instance-class network type support.
- SPARQL (services/neptune/sparql, served on the cluster port in embedded and docker modes): not produced or consumed are JSON-LD, TriX, RDF4J-binary and binary-results-table media types (Accept for them returns 406 UnsupportedMediaTypeException, code and status unverified); SPARQL LOAD reads only S3 URLs (s3:// and https://s3*.amazonaws.com), not arbitrary http(s) sources; SERVICE federation, SPARQL-star and Neptune's SPARQL query hints are rejected with MalformedQueryException; REDUCED is treated as DISTINCT; decimals use exact rationals, integer literals beyond 64 bits fail InvalidNumericDataException as documented (decimal and floating point widths are not bounded), other numeric widths fold to xsd:integer/xsd:double results.
- UNVERIFIED (errors-engine-codes.html lists no UnsupportedMediaTypeException, no 415 or 406 status and no not-found code for a missing graph; its list is the only documented set of engine codes): the empty 200 body returned by a successful SPARQL update, the 415/406 error codes for unsupported request/Accept media types, 404 NotFound-style errors for missing Graph Store graphs, the 'Max concurrent load limit breached' message and DELETE templates without GRAPH or WITH targeting only the DefaultNamedGraph rather than every graph (the docs state the DefaultNamedGraph fallback for loading, inserting and updating triples without a named graph target).
- Bulk loader (/loader): iamRoleArn is required (MissingParameterException) but never assumed, and mode (NEW/RESUME/AUTO) and parallelism are validated against load-api-reference-load.html but otherwise ignored: RESUME and AUTO do not look for a previous job from the same source, every job is a fresh NEW run (runNumber 1) and parallelism does not size a thread pool; SSE-KMS permission checks and write-conflict statuses (LOAD_DATA_DEADLOCK, LOAD_COMMIT_FAILED...) are not modelled; loader job history is in memory only and is not captured by Snapshot/Restore (loaded triples and graph data are). RDF: datatypeMismatchErrors and insertErrors always report 0. Property-graph CSV (csv, opencypher): Date/DateTime values are stored as UTC ISO-8601 strings because the property store has no temporal value (Neptune stores epoch time); Float values are widened to Double; ID spaces (:ID(space)) only qualify the header, a node id repeated in two spaces merges into one node; quoted-empty and blank ~id/:ID values are a parsing error; the exact datatype-mismatch error wording, totalRecords for edge rows and recordNum numbering are unverified; edge files without a ~label/:TYPE column default the label to edge.
- Port speaks plain HTTP/WebSocket and unencrypted Bolt, not TLS. SPARQL explain returns a text/html rendering of this engine's own algebra, not Neptune's operator table. Neptune's SPARQL stream, statistics and engine-status endpoints are not served. With NEPTUNE_GREMLIN=container (docker mode only) Gremlin runs in a stock tinkerpop/gremlin-server container whose graph is separate from the in-process openCypher/Bolt graph (the default in-process mode shares one graph). The RDF store is always separate from the property graph, as in Neptune.
- Bolt: explicit transactions hold the cluster graph exclusively until COMMIT/ROLLBACK/disconnect, and results are materialised before PULL streaming. Not smoke-tested against a real neo4j driver (none available on the dev box); proven by the pkgs/bolt protocol tests and the neptune bolt_front_test.go.
- openCypher subset (services/neptune/opencypher): CALL, FOREACH, LOAD CSV and shortestPath/allShortestPaths are rejected with UnsupportedOperationException, matching feature-opencypher-compliance.html (CALL[YIELD], shortestPath and allShortestPaths are listed as not supported; FOREACH and LOAD CSV are not listed as supported). UNION/UNION ALL are read-only as documented (an updating part returns UnsupportedOperationException). UNVERIFIED (not named on the Neptune compliance page, implemented from the openCypher 9 spec): list comprehensions, pattern predicates in WHERE and size() of a pattern. Not matching Neptune: the ^ operator, which Neptune documents as unsupported, is evaluated; temporal/spatial types and constraints are not implemented.
- NEPTUNE_GREMLIN=container: the Gremlin graph in the container is not captured by cluster snapshots or persistence; relaunched clusters start with an empty Gremlin graph. The stock gremlin-server image exposes no snapshot API other than the io() step, which writes to the container filesystem (GraphSON/GraphML) and would need a file copy out and back in on every snapshot; not implemented because the capture could not be verified against a running container on this box. In the default in-process mode the single shared graph is persisted. The writer and reader endpoints are the same host:port.
- Gremlin subset (services/neptune/gremlin): lambdas, meta-properties, withSack split/merge functions (a withSack merge Operator is accepted but inert: no traverser bulking), barrier(normSack), GraphBinary encoding of subgraph() results (a Graph has no GraphBinary type here; GraphBinary clients get a 599 serialization error and must request GraphSON, TinkerPop's own GraphBinary has no Graph serializer either, unverified), the 3.8 one-by()-only errors for sack()/sample()/dedup() (sample() enforces it), Neptune support for index() (absent from the Neptune step pages, implemented anyway) and the exact error text of math()/sack() failures (recalled, unverified), g.tx() inside a script string (Neptune also rejects it: manual transactions are bytecode-only), profile/explain and variable assignment in scripts are not implemented and return MalformedQueryException/UnsupportedOperationException. Sessions: a session holds the whole graph exclusively while a transaction is open (Neptune uses MVCC, so concurrent readers are not blocked there), all open sessions of a dropped WebSocket are rolled back, and a failed request rolls back the open transaction but keeps the session. The string steps (toLower, toUpper, trim, lTrim, rTrim, length, asString, split, concat, replace, substring) are TinkerPop 3.7.1+ and are enabled for every engine version; the first Neptune engine release carrying them is unverified. Integer and float widths are folded to Int64/Double on write; property cardinality is single (list/set stored as a list value); vertex property ids are derived, not stored.

### Structural gaps

These do not block an A grade — no implementation could produce real data here because the underlying data source cannot exist in an emulator.

- DescribeDBClusterSnapshots IncludePublic/IncludeShared add other accounts' snapshots; single-account emulator, so there are none to add (SnapshotType=public/shared are evaluated).
- DeleteDBInstance SkipFinalSnapshot=false creates no snapshot: Neptune has no DB-instance snapshot resource in the pinned SDK.
